name: Cabezo de la Plata & Puerto San Pedro
surfaceTxt: Secondary roads, service roads & cycle paths
summary: Inland roads where Valverde trains — the club-run classic from San Javier through the Campo de Murcia hills.
desc: Road bike route along secondary roads, service roads and cycle paths where you can sometimes spot a world champion like Alejandro Valverde training. Rolls inland through the Campo de Murcia to Cabezo de la Plata, coming home past the port at San Pedro del Pinatar.

name: Canal del Trasvase — Río Seco
summary: Traffic-free gravel along the Trasvase canal service track out to the Río Seco rambla.
desc: Route for MTB, hybrid or gravel bikes following the path parallel to the Tajo–Segura transfer canal — pan-flat, arrow-straight farm tracks through the Campo de Cartagena out to the Río Seco and back. Zero traffic, big skies.

name: Trasvase & Vía Verde del Campo de Cartagena
summary: The big gravel link-up: canal service tracks joining the Vía Verde greenway across the Campo.
desc: MTB/hybrid/gravel route that follows the transfer-canal track before joining the Vía Verde del Campo de Cartagena — the disused-railway greenway. A long, satisfying gravel day linking the region’s two best traffic-free corridors.

name: Garrucha & Cresta del Gallo
summary: The mountain day: the Garrucha climb and Murcia’s famous Cresta del Gallo, back via Cabezo de la Plata.
desc: Road bike route with real climbing — up the Garrucha and over the famous Cresta del Gallo above Murcia city, then back to San Javier via Cabezo de la Plata. The biggest climbing day in the local repertoire; the Cresta is a Vuelta regular.

name: Mar Menor Loop (with the Ferry)
surfaceTxt: Coast roads + La Manga + lagoon ferry
summary: Circle the whole Mar Menor, taking the ferry across the lagoon mouth — a ride with a boat in the middle.
desc: Road or hybrid route around the Mar Menor that uses the ferry to hop across the lagoon, linking La Manga back to the mainland. Flat, hugely scenic, and the boat leg makes it feel like a proper adventure.

name: Mar Menor MTB (Ferry)
summary: Gravel/MTB on the spectacular shoreline paths that border the lagoon, ferry home across the mouth.
desc: MTB or gravel loop on the shoreline paths that border the Mar Menor — sandy tracks, salt-flats scenery and flamingos — taking the ferry to close the loop. The prettiest off-road ride on the lagoon.

name: El Rebate Climb
summary: Quiet roads and constant rollers from San Miguel de Salinas up to the El Rebate climb.
desc: Road route on very quiet lanes into the continuously rolling terrain around San Miguel de Salinas, leading to the El Rebate climb — a steady, honest test that wintering pros use for tempo work.

name: Salinas & Arenales de San Pedro
summary: Easy gravel through the salt-pans park — dunes, windmills and flamingos.
desc: A quiet MTB/gravel outing through the Salinas y Arenales de San Pedro del Pinatar regional park — salt pans, dunes and flamingos on flat sandy tracks. Perfect recovery-day scenery, straight off the northern promenade.

name: Cuestas del Cedacero & Batería Castillitos
summary: The epic: over the Cedacero climbs to the Castillitos gun battery, 250 m above the sea.
desc: Cycling route for road bikes to the Cartagena region via the Canal del Trasvase, then up the Cuestas del Cedacero and the dramatic cliff road to the Batería de Castillitos — the 1930s fortress perched 250 m above the Mediterranean. The hardest, most spectacular road day here.

name: Campo de Cartagena Loop (Dolores de Pacheco)
summary: The local training staple — a flat, fast farmland loop through Dolores de Pacheco.
desc: The classic campo circuit: dead-flat, near-traffic-free farm lanes west through the market gardens to Dolores de Pacheco and back. Big skies, fast tarmac — perfect for a chaingang or an easy spin. Traced from a real recorded ride.

name: La Unión Out & Back (Road)
summary: South across the campo to the historic mining town of La Unión — the road-bike version of the Sierra Minera trip.
desc: Cross the Campo de Cartagena on quiet farm roads to La Unión, the old mining town beneath the ochre Sierra Minera. A steady climb past Roche earns the views; the return is fast and flat. Traced from a real recorded ride.

name: Los Nietos & the South Shore
summary: The southern shore of the Mar Menor — Los Urrutias, Los Nietos and a chiringuito stop on the water.
desc: Follow the lagoon’s quieter southern shore through Los Urrutias and Estrella de Mar to Los Nietos, where a rustic beach bar sits right on the water. Flat all day and glorious in the winter sun. Traced from a real recorded ride.

name: Avileses Inland Loop
summary: Gently rolling lanes northwest into the orchard country around Avileses.
desc: Head inland away from the coast tourists never leave: rolling, quiet lanes through citrus and almond country to the village of Avileses and back. Honest, pretty riding with barely a car. Traced from a real recorded ride.

name: Northern Hills Epic (toward Ricote)
surfaceTxt: Mountain roads — a genuine big day
summary: The big one: deep into the Murcian hills toward the Ricote valley. Bring food, water and ambition.
desc: A proper epic north-west into the mountains of Murcia toward the palm-lined Ricote valley — long climbs, remote roads and nearly 2,000 m of altitude before the long run home across the campo. The hardest suggested ride here. Traced from a real recorded ride.

name: Pilar de la Horadada Out & Back
summary: An easy northbound spin on the inland lanes to Pilar de la Horadada.
desc: A short, friendly ride north on the quiet lanes that parallel the coast, turning at Pilar de la Horadada. Ideal first ride of a trip or coffee-shop tempo. Traced from a real recorded ride.

name: La Vuelta 2026 · Stage 11 — Cartagena → Lorca
summary: The exact roads the Vuelta a España raced on 2 Sep 2026 — out of Cartagena, up the Mar Menor past Los Alcázares, then west over the Alto de Aledo to Lorca.
desc: Stage 11 of the 2026 Vuelta a España (Wednesday 2 September, 153.8 km): the peloton rolled out of Cartagena, ran up the Mar Menor coast past Los Alcázares — right through our patch — then struck west across the Campo de Cartagena, over the Category-3 Alto de Aledo with ~30 km to go, to a bunch sprint in Lorca. This is the official race line, straight from La Vuelta’s own Komoot track. A big day at 154 km, but any section is tarmac the pros raced on.
